title: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025
note: Undated 40-question theory paper with yellow-highlighted supplied answers. 4 September 2025 is a posting date, not a verified exam date. All highlights were read from the original color PDF and are preserved separately from independently audited keys. This paper begins with parasympathetic bronchoconstriction and is not the 29-question anatomy-first version.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of parasympathetic nervous system activation on airways?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Parasympathetic vagal acetylcholine causes bronchoconstriction; bronchodilation is associated with beta-adrenergic stimulation.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 1; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which of the following occur during normal inspiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Quiet inspiration is driven principally by diaphragmatic contraction. Internal intercostals are chiefly recruited for forceful expiration, not the principal inspiratory action.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 2; source page 1.

questions.prompt: which one the following can’t be directly measured by spirometry ؟
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Residual volume cannot be exhaled into a simple spirometer, whereas tidal and reserve volumes can be recorded.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 3; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which gas is used for estimating of “diffusing capacity of O2” in the lung?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Carbon monoxide uptake is used to estimate diffusing capacity because hemoglobin binding keeps capillary CO partial pressure very low. Source Q19 repeats the same stem with reordered choices; both source records are preserved.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 4; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following muscles has a role in deep expiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Abdominal recti help force expiration by increasing abdominal pressure and pushing the diaphragm upward. The other listed muscles assist inspiration.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 5; source page 1.

questions.prompt: What is the amount of Transpulmonary pressure at the beginning of normal inspiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At normal end expiration/start inspiration, Palv is about 0 and Ppl about -5 cm H2O, so transpulmonary pressure Palv - Ppl is approximately +5 cm H2O.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 6; source page 1.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of surfactant on lung compliance?
options: It depends on the amount of pleural pressure
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant lowers alveolar surface tension and increases lung compliance.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 7; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is the “Residual volume”?
options: The volume of air remaining in the lungs after the most forceful expiration
The maximum amount of air a person can expel from the lungs after first filling the lungs to their maximum extent
The amount of air that remains in the lungs at the end of normal expiration
The maximum extra volume of air that can be expired by forceful expiration
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Residual volume is the gas remaining after maximal forced expiration. Gas remaining after a normal expiration is FRC.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 8; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which zone of the lung has blood flow during both systole and diastole phases in standing position?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In zone 3, both pulmonary arterial and venous pressures exceed alveolar pressure, so flow persists through systole and diastole.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 9; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which one the following decreases the affinity of hemoglobin for O2?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increased temperature shifts the dissociation curve right and reduces oxygen affinity. Higher pH and lower CO2/BPG shift it left.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 10; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is the “anatomical shunt”?
options: Mixture of pulmonary vein blood and bronchial vein blood
Increasing of VA/Q ratio 2.5 times more than normal amount
Mixture of pulmonary arterial and venous blood
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Bronchial venous blood draining into pulmonary veins creates normal anatomical venous admixture. V/Q = 0 describes a perfused but unventilated unit, a functional shunt mechanism rather than this anatomical bypass.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 11; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What changes are happened in the breathing pattern by increasing the activity of the pneumotaxic center?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the traditional model, stronger pneumotaxic inspiratory switch-off shortens inspiration and tends to increase respiratory frequency.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 12; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which one is correct about ventilation and perfusion in the lungs?
options: The blood flow decreases from the top of the lung to bottom
The ventilation to perfusion ratio (V/Q) increases from top of the lung to bottom
The ventilation increases from the top of the lung to the bottom
V/Q ratio is same for all levels of the lung in upright person
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In an upright healthy lung, absolute ventilation increases toward the base. Perfusion increases even more, so V/Q decreases toward the base.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 13; source page 3.

questions.prompt: What is the normal value of CO2 pressure in systemic arterial blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional resting systemic arterial PCO2 is approximately 40 mmHg; mixed venous PCO2 is approximately 45 mmHg.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 14; source page 3.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum amount of CO2 transportation in the blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The largest fraction of CO2 is transported as bicarbonate. Carbaminohemoglobin is distinct from carboxyhemoglobin, which involves carbon monoxide.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 15; source page 3.

questions.prompt: What is the normal value of utilization coefficient for O2 in a normal condition?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The standard resting example extracts 5 mL O2 from 20 mL O2/dL delivered: utilization coefficient = 5/20 = 25%.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 16; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which one is correct about the role of the dorsal respiratory group in medulla?
options: Inhibits the pneumotaxic center in pons
Sends its action potential to phrenic nerves
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The traditional DRG account describes inspiratory output to phrenic motor pathways. It is not first activated only for deep inspiration; normal rhythm is generated by an interacting medullary network.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 17; source page 3.

questions.prompt: In a patient with pulmonary fibrosis, for a pressure difference of 4 mm Hg between the two sides of the respiratory membrane, the amount of 400 ml of CO2 is exchanged per minute, what will be the diffusing capacity of this gas?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Diffusing capacity = gas transfer per minute / pressure gradient = 400/4 = 100 mL/min/mmHg. The gas is CO2 here; no O2/CO2 conversion is required.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 18; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which gas is used for estimating of “diffusing capacity of O2” in the lung?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO is the diffusion-test gas. This is a within-source repeat of Q4 with the correct answer moved from A to B; both original source numbers remain traceable.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 19; source page 4.

questions.prompt: What is the normal pleural pressure at the beginning and end of normal expiration, respectively?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Source highlight C is incorrect for the printed expiration stem. At the beginning of expiration pleural pressure is about -7.5 cm H2O; it returns toward -5 at the end. Thus A is the audited answer; C would describe inspiration.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 20; source page 4.

questions.prompt: How much cilia are there on each epithelial cell in the mucociliary system in airways?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The highlighted 200 is the intended approximate order of magnitude. Counts vary by source and airway region; the local histology review gives about 250-300 cilia per ciliated columnar cell. It is not an exact universal count, but the other choices differ by orders of magnitude.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 21; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following respiratory works is less than others?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Withheld: the source highlights airway-resistance work, but the conventional quiet-breathing teaching comparison makes tissue-resistance work the smallest component. The stem does not specify breathing conditions, and the local review verifies definitions rather than an invariant ranking. Retain the disputed supplied B without forcing a scored answer.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 22; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Where are there club cells?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Club cells are nonciliated secretory cells of bronchiolar epithelium, especially terminal bronchioles.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 23; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which type of these cells is the most or least in microscopic structure of the respiratory epithelium?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Read the awkward 'most or least' wording as the paired most-and-least populations: ciliated columnar cells are most numerous and small-granule/Kulchitsky cells are a sparse neuroendocrine population. The source's spelling Kolchitsky is preserved.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 24; source page 5.

questions.prompt: In the histological structure of the trachea................
options: All epithelial cells have acidophilic granules.
The C-shaped cartilage covered by perichondrium.
Serous glands in the lamina propria produce mucus.
Hyaline C-shaped cartilage is lined by epithelium.
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Tracheal C-shaped hyaline cartilage is covered by perichondrium. Serous cells do not produce mucus, and epithelium does not directly line the cartilage.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 25; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which of these structures are lined by 2 types of epithelia?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Epiglottis shows nonkeratinized stratified squamous and respiratory epithelial regions; the transition varies on the laryngeal surface.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 26; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which of these cells have a defense role in lung?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The supplied highlight C ('Pneumococcus Type III') is not a valid lung-cell identity. The source appears to misuse pneumococcus/pneumocyte terminology, which is preserved in the choices. Club cells genuinely contribute antimicrobial secretion and local defense, so D is the defensible answer as printed; this is not a silent substitution of macrophage for C.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 27; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is TRUE about the Canalicular period?
options: The alveolar ducts will start forming at this period.
The epithelium of the terminal bronchi becomes very thick.
Capillaries begin to bulge at this period.
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Withheld: A (alveolar ducts form) is true, but B can also be true near the late canalicular period with intensive support. The stage spans many weeks and the stem gives no age or treatment context. The highlighted A is preserved as supplied, but cannot uniquely exclude B.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 28; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which of the following linings does the laryngotracheal diverticulum give rise to the muscles & Glands of the respiratory system, respectively?
options: The mesoderm of 5th and 6th pair of pharyngeal arches
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Respiratory muscles/supporting tissues are mesodermal, while glandular epithelium is endodermal. The diverticulum itself does not give rise to every mesodermal tissue; B captures the intended paired lineages despite the imprecise stem. Laryngeal muscles relate to fourth and sixth arches, not fifth and sixth.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 29; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Bifurcation of trachea is at the level of ....
options: Intervertebral disc between T4 and T5
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The tracheal bifurcation is conventionally at the sternal-angle/T4-T5 level. The source's unlettered separate final line '5th intercostal space' is restored as fourth option D, not merged with xiphoid process.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 30; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is innervated by external laryngeal nerve?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: External laryngeal nerve supplies cricothyroid; the other listed intrinsic muscles receive recurrent laryngeal motor innervation.

questions.prompt: Where is the inferior border of the lung in the mid-clavicular line?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The inferior lung border crosses the sixth rib at the midclavicular line; parietal pleura descends to the eighth rib there.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 32; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Maxillary sinus drains into the ...
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The maxillary sinus drains through the semilunar hiatus into the middle meatus.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 33; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which one is a branch of the maxillary artery?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Sphenopalatine is the terminal maxillary-artery branch supplying the nasal cavity.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 34; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Galen anastomosis under piriform recess is formed by ...
options: Internal laryngeal and external laryngeal nerves
Internal laryngeal and recurrent laryngeal nerves
External laryngeal and recurrent laryngeal nerves
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Galen's anastomosis connects internal laryngeal with recurrent/inferior laryngeal branches behind the larynx. The local review includes the labelled original laryngeal-nerve diagram.

questions.prompt: Which nerve does supply sensory innervation of the larynx from laryngeal inlet to vocal folds?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Internal laryngeal provides sensory supply from the laryngeal inlet to the vocal-fold level; recurrent/inferior laryngeal supplies the region below the folds.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 36; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Mediastinal pleura is innervated by ...
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Mediastinal parietal pleura is supplied by phrenic nerves; costal and peripheral diaphragmatic pleura receive intercostal innervation.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 37; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which bone on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity is a separate bone of the facial skeleton?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Inferior nasal concha is a separate facial bone; superior and middle conchae belong to the ethmoid.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 38; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Where is the location of the palatine tonsil?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Palatine tonsil lies in the lateral oropharyngeal wall between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches.

evidence: Respiratory theory key - undated, posted 4 September 2025; printed question 39; source page 8.

questions.prompt: Which one is formed by Inferior free border of the quadrangular membrane?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The inferior free border of the quadrangular membrane forms the vestibular ligament; the superior free border of conus elasticus forms the vocal ligament.

audit.notes: All eight original color PDF pages visually inspected. All 40 numbered source questions and all 40 yellow highlights retained. Highlights are unofficial providedKey evidence, not automatic grading authority. Q20 corrected C to A for the printed expiration wording; Q27 corrected invalid cell-name C to actual defensive Club-cell option D. Q22 and Q28 are deliberately ungraded. Q30 has four visible separate choices, with the unlettered fourth line normalized as D; Q23-27 assigned histology and Q28-29 embryology. No key from this paper was applied to another paper. Q4 and Q19 are a same-stem within-source repeat with different option order, both retained for source traceability.
